stories.situation: Northbeam's order-processing monolith ran on Java 8 with a single deploy pipeline, so a change to any of the 40 backend services required a full regression pass and blocked releases for up to 3 days.
stories.behavior: Split the monolith into Java and Spring Boot microservices behind Kafka topics, giving each of the 6 core services its own deploy pipeline and contract tests.
stories.impact: Release conflicts across teams fell 60% and a routine change now ships in under a day instead of 3.

stories.situation: Each new backend service at Northbeam took 2 weeks to bootstrap because there was no shared framework for auth, logging, or health checks.
stories.behavior: Built a Spring Boot starter library with shared auth, structured logging, and health-check endpoints, and rolled it out across 8 services.
stories.impact: New-service bootstrap time dropped from 2 weeks to 3 days, and every service now reports consistent health metrics.

stories.situation: Order status updates were polled from PostgreSQL every 30 seconds by 5 downstream services, adding load and a 30-second lag to shipping notifications.
stories.behavior: Introduced a Kafka topic for order-status events, migrating the 5 downstream services from polling to event consumption with idempotent handlers.
stories.impact: Notification lag dropped from 30 seconds to under 2 seconds and PostgreSQL polling load fell 70%.

stories.situation: The order database saw repeated reads of the same cart and pricing data, and PostgreSQL p95 read latency climbed to 900ms during Northbeam's peak shipping weeks.
stories.behavior: Added a Redis cache in front of the cart and pricing reads with a 5-minute TTL and a cache-invalidation hook on writes.
stories.impact: p95 read latency fell 45% and PostgreSQL CPU usage dropped 30% during the next peak week.

stories.situation: All 12 backend services deployed from a hand-maintained set of AWS EC2 AMIs, and a new service took 3 days to onboard because the AMI build was manual.
stories.behavior: Containerized all 12 services with Docker, standardized the base image, and moved deployment to AWS ECS with a shared Terraform module for the task definitions.
stories.impact: New-service onboarding dropped from 3 days to half a day and every service now runs the same base image.

stories.situation: Provisioning a new environment for a backend service at Northbeam meant an engineer clicking through the AWS console for 2 days, and configuration drifted between environments.
stories.behavior: Wrote Terraform modules covering the AWS networking, ECS task definitions, and IAM roles for a distributed systems footprint of 6 services and 3 databases, and put every change through a pull-request plan review.
stories.impact: New-environment setup dropped from 2 days to 2 hours and configuration drift between environments went to zero.

stories.situation: Anchor's analytics warehouse ran a full-table PostgreSQL refresh every night, and the 200GB job routinely ran past the 6-hour maintenance window into business hours.
stories.behavior: Rebuilt the load in Python and SQL around incremental change data capture (CDC) from the PostgreSQL source tables, replacing the nightly full refresh.
stories.impact: The load window dropped from 6 hours to 45 minutes and the warehouse was never late again during my 2 years there.

stories.situation: The 15 slowest queries in the analytics warehouse were responsible for most of the 12-second average dashboard load time that 8 downstream teams complained about.
stories.behavior: Profiled execution plans for the 15 slowest queries and rewrote them with better join order, targeted indexes, and query optimization to cut redundant table scans.
stories.impact: Average dashboard load time fell from 12 seconds to 2 seconds across all 8 downstream teams.

stories.situation: Anchor's 6 internal REST APIs for finance and marketing were built ad hoc, with no shared test suite, and reporting bugs reached support every week.
stories.behavior: Rewrote the APIs in Python with a shared routing layer, well-tested code at 90% branch coverage, and a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline gating every merge.
stories.impact: Reporting bugs escalated to support dropped 50% quarter over quarter and every API shipped through the same test gate.

stories.situation: Downstream teams pulled from Anchor's PostgreSQL analytics tables directly, so a schema change in the source could silently corrupt 3 finance dashboards overnight.
stories.behavior: Introduced change data capture (CDC) as the contract between the source PostgreSQL tables and 8 downstream teams, with a documented star schema behind it.
stories.impact: Zero silent schema breaks in the 18 months after rollout, down from 2 incidents the year before.

stories.situation: Anchor's data pipelines shipped through a manual deploy checklist, and a release could go out with an untested query change since nothing blocked the merge.
stories.behavior: Set up a GitHub Actions CI/CD pipeline that ran the test suite, linted SQL migrations, and blocked merges on a failing check for all 6 internal APIs.
stories.impact: Untested changes reaching the data pipelines dropped to zero and code review turnaround for the team fell from 2 days to same-day.

stories.situation: Fielding's sales and support teams requested new client-reporting metrics through email, and each of the 12 recurring requests took a full sprint of engineering time to turn into a spreadsheet.
stories.behavior: Did cross-functional work with sales and support to scope a self-serve dashboard, then built it in React so non-engineers could add a metric without a ticket.
stories.impact: The 12 recurring spreadsheet requests became a self-serve dashboard, freeing roughly a sprint of engineering time a month.

stories.situation: The self-serve reporting dashboard's charting was slow to load and support kept a spreadsheet backup because they didn't trust it.
stories.behavior: Rewrote the dashboard's data-fetching layer in JavaScript with incremental loading and wrote well-tested code, covering 85% of branches with pytest on the Python API behind it, following test-driven development practices throughout.
stories.impact: Dashboard load time fell from 9 seconds to under 2 seconds and support retired the spreadsheet backup within a month.

stories.situation: New hires on Morgan's team spent their first 2 days searching 500 internal wiki pages to answer basic setup questions, and the same questions kept coming up on the team channel.
stories.behavior: Built DocQuery, a Python service that embeds the wiki pages in a Postgres vector extension and answers questions through an LLM API, so a new hire can ask in plain language instead of searching.
stories.impact: Onboarding-question turnaround for 15 new hires dropped from about 2 days to the same day, and repeat channel questions fell noticeably.
